chemicals.concentration_notes: Concentrated mainly in the roots and bark.
chemicals.description: A phenolic compound that causes gastrointestinal irritation.
chemicals.name: Paeonol

description:
Peony (Paeonia spp.) is a popular garden plant and beautiful cut flower, but it is mildly toxic to cats. The plant contains chemicals like paeonol and paeoniflorin that can upset a cat's stomach. These compounds are found in all parts of the plant, including the roots, bark, flowers, and leaves, with the highest amounts in the roots.

If a cat chews or eats parts of a peony, the plant chemicals can irritate their digestive system. Even cut peony flowers kept in a vase indoors can be a risk for curious cats.

Most of the time, the symptoms are mild. A cat might drool, vomit, have diarrhea, or seem a bit tired and low on energy. These issues usually clear up on their own, but it is best to keep peonies out of reach. Please contact a veterinarian if your cat's symptoms are severe or do not improve.
emergencyNote: Remove the Hazard and Contact the Vet: Immediately take the cat away from the plant and call your veterinarian for advice. Do not wait for severe symptoms to develop
name: Peony
safetyNotes: Toxic compounds: paeonol and paeoniflorin (phenolic compounds); roots contain the highest concentration
Mechanism: paeonol and paeoniflorin irritate the GI mucosa; high doses may have mild CNS effects
Symptoms: vomiting, diarrhea, drooling; typically mild and self-limiting
All parts are mildly toxic, though the root is most concentrated; cut peony flowers in a vase are also a risk
Symptoms are usually mild; consult your vet if symptoms are severe or persistent

treatments.name: Remove the Hazard and Contact the Vet: Immediately take the cat away from the plant and call your veterinarian for advice. Do not wait for severe symptoms to develop
Do Not Induce Vomiting: Do not attempt to make your cat sick at home unless explicitly instructed to do so by a professional, as it may not be helpful and can sometimes cause further harm
Collect Samples: If possible, take a sample of the plant—and a sample of the cat's vomit, if they have thrown up—to the veterinary clinic to help with the diagnosis
